Explicit accepted primary source/body reading reused with matching pins. Waterhouse memorandum dated after March 2, 1855 from a Wollaston exchange, with raw year-end bound; no exact March day chosen. Full list covers tarsal counts and sex differences in Anisotomidae, Cryptophagidae, Mycetophagidae and Staphylinidae, with continuations and ditto marks tied to their correct rows. Male/female symbols and counts are substantive. Raw diag/ramme debris and flattened layout are retained in the source projection. Darwin separate note, later chapter label and Origin quotations must not inherit the memorandum date or Waterhouse voice. The bibliographic entry under Wollaston does not itself authenticate the relevant letter or book. This tarsal list is not the missing atlas text discussed in 1641.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1641: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. March 4, 1855 follows a missing Waterhouse note claiming the atlas text should be present. Darwin has searched each page, insists the text is absent from the parcel, and distinguishes maps currently studied from maps and text previously seen at the Athenaeum. A future copy is offered, not received. Carboniferous/Silurian mammals are his hope, not known discoveries. Province without rodents refers to atlas geography, not the tarsal memorandum 1625. Published 1856 edition and later pamphlet possession must not replace the missing contemporary text. No surviving immediate incoming prompt.

record_notes.DCP-LETT-1713: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. July 8, 1855 is supported by endorsement. Darwin asks for an accessible systematic British Lepidoptera guide for his sons, preferring learning from descriptions to mere collecting or pictures. Distinguish the limitations he finds in Stephens, Westwood synopsis, and the magnificent Humphreys/Westwood loan from John Lubbock. The postscript qualifies that Stephens works reasonably for butterflies; book identity in the footnote is probable, not certain. These are initiated questions, not a reply to earlier fossil or tarsal correspondence.
